label: weak: copy-phase output o/m/x, or early original y/0 (low precision)
explanation: Sparse (about 1% of steps) with diffuse, low-precision structure. About 64% of activation mass is in the copy/delimiter phase, enriched when the token being output is o (14x lift), m (10x) or x (6x), and somewhat at recall_idx 2-4. Even so, only about 14% of o-output steps fire. About 30% of mass is in the original phase at t=1-3, mostly when the input is y or 0. It never fires at t=0 and rarely at original positions 4 and up. The best disjunction reaches mass recall 0.74 on dev but precision is only about 0.10 (F1 0.17). Restricting by input token or recall position did not raise precision meaningfully, so what decides firing within these contexts is still unknown. Strongest top examples output o right after input t (e.g. b d t o ... <DEL> b d [t]).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (copy phase: o, m, x, e; delimiter step: o, x, e, m; input phase: ) and the next token to output (most: o, m, r, d, x, e; least: 3, j, l, c); timing cues that raise it most: t=1, t=2, L=4 & t=6.
